violations.title: Chemical Sanitizing, Contact Time Met
violations.observation: The CONCENTRATION OF CHLORINE SANITIZER SOLUTION IN THE 3 COMPARTMENT SINK IS TOO LOW FOR SANITIZING.. Equipment, food- contact surfaces, and utensils are therefore not adequately sanitized after cleaning. CHLORINE SANITIZER SOLUTION CONCENTRATION MEASURED AT <10 PPM AT TIME OF INSPECTION..
violations.corrective_action: EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS PROVIDED GUIDANCE TO PIC IN ADJUSTING AND TESTING CHLORINE SANITIZER SOLUTION IN 3 COMPARTMENT SINK TO MEET 50-200 PPM DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: KAMPOW SAUCE AT 131F IN WARMER IN FRONT SERVICE AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REHEAT FOODS TO 165F OR ABOVE FOR HOT HOLDING AT 135F OR ABOVE.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: MIXED GREENS AT 63F IN ICE BATH IN FRONT SERVICE AREA; RAW CHICKEN AT 63F IN ICE BATH IN KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED TO PIC TO TRANSFER RAW CHICKEN TO FREEZER FOR RAPID COOLING TO 41F AND MAINTAIN IN REFRIGERATOR. PIC WILL. DISCARD UNUSED OR UNSOLD PORTIONS OF MIXED GREENS IN FRONT SERVICE AT 6:00 PM

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: COOKED CHICKEN DUMPLINGS, SEASONED ICE, GREEN CURRY, STICKY RICE, COOKED CHICKEN ALL PREPARED AND HELD FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS IN TRUE 2 DOOR UPRIGHT REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO APPLY APPROPRIATE DATE MARKING DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. OBSERVED EMPLOYEE ENTER THE KITCHEN AND BEGAN TO WEAR GLOVES TO ENGAGE IN FOOD PREPARATION WITHOUT WASHING HANDS.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO REMOVE GLOVES AND WASH HANDS BEFORE APPLYING CLEAN GLOVES TO BEGIN FOOD PREPARATION. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEE TRAINING AND COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a food preparation sink, warewashing sink or in a mop sink: 3 COMPARTMENT SINK
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO WASH HANDS AT HANDWASHING SINK ONLY. PLEASE ENSURE EMPLOYEE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. OBSERVED CHICKEN BROTH AT 117F FOR 5 HOURS IN DEEP COVERED POT IN TRUE 2 DOOR UPRIGHT REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD CHICKEN BROTH DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS ARE COOLED FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS USING PROPER COOLING METHODS.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED STICKY RICE AND GREEN CURRY PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN TRUE 2 DOOR UPRIGHT REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC APPLIED APPROPRIATE DATE MARKING DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE. AH LENG (Inspection Date: 01/16/2026) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: OBSERVED CHICKEN BROTH AT 117F FOR 5 HOURS IN DEEP COVERED POT IN TRUE 2 DOOR UPRIGHT REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. CHICKEN BROTH WAS DISCARDED DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE SMALLER PORTIONS, ICE BATHS AND ICE WANDS IN FREEZER TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS TO THE PROPER COOLING PARAMETERS. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the BASE OF KITCHEN BACK DOOR.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE INSTALL DOOR SWEEP AT BASE OF KITCHEN DOOR TO PREVENT ENTRY TO PESTS. PLEASE EMAIL EHS ONCE DOOR SWEEP HAS BEEN INSTALLED.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED RICE AND OIL STORED DIRECTLY ON FLOOR IN KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS TO ELEVATE FOODS TO AT LEAST 6 INCHES OFF THE FLOOR.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed that clean KITCHEN EQUIPMENT were stored in a manner that exposed the item(s) to contamination: DIRECTLY ON FLOOR UNDER HANDWASHING SINK.
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS FOR STORAGE OF EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): TO STORE UTENSILS.
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS FOR STORAGE OF EQUIPMENT AND UTENSILS.
